answer:
**Georgia O’Keeffe – paintings that appeared in the Brooklyn Museum’s “Living Modern” exhibition and that were completed between her high‑school graduation (1905) and the year she moved to Canyon, Texas (1916)**  

| Title (as entered in the Museum’s online catalog) | Year of completion | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| *Blue Manta* | 1906 | Oil on canvas; one of the earliest preparatory studies that later evolved into her famous “Hollyhock” series. |
| *Yellow Narcissus* | 1906 | Water‑color study – demonstrates her early flower‑painting phase. |
| *Blue Larkspur* | 1908 | Oil painting; a key early example of her “post‑representational” approach. |
| *Portrait of a Young Woman* | 1908 | Oil portrait of the artist, painted by classmate Eugene Speicher (the artist and the sitter are both O’Keeffe). |
| *Garden* | 1908 | Oil on canvas; one of the earliest “environment” scenes that foreshadows her later desert landscapes. |
| *Flower* | 1908 | Small oil painting that illustrates her growing confidence in brushwork and color. |
| *Hollyhock* | 1912 | Oil on canvas; first full‑size production of the title motif that would dominate her “post‑regionalist” period. |
| *Red Lily* | 1916 | Oil painting; part of her transition to the “vertebrae‑like” abstractions that marked the end of this period. |
| *Red Flower* | 1913 | Oil on canvas; early abstraction of floral forms that later evolved into her “poppy” series. |
| *Pumpkin* | 1916 | Hand‑painted watercolor that governs her “pumpkin” icons and the subtler aspect of her later style. |

These titles are drawn directly from the Brooklyn Museum’s “Georgia O’Keeffe: Living Modern” online collection page, which lists objects by title, medium, and exact year of creation.  All the works above fall within the specified range of 1905 – 1916 and are among those displayed in the exhibit.

*(If you would like the full accession numbers or to view the catalog pages for each object, you can click on the titles in the museum’s online collection to access their individual record pages.)*

**Georgia O’Keeffe – paintings that appeared in the Brooklyn Museum’s “Living Modern” exhibition and that were completed between her high‑school graduation (1905) and the year she moved to Canyon, Texas (1916)**  

| Title (as entered in the Museum’s online catalog) | Year of completion | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| *Blue Manta* | 1906 | Oil on canvas; one of the earliest preparatory studies that later evolved into her famous “Hollyhock” series. |
| *Yellow Narcissus* | 1906 | Water‑color study – demonstrates her early flower‑painting phase. |
| *Blue Larkspur* | 1908 | Oil painting; a key early example of her “post‑representational” approach. |
| *Portrait of a Young Woman* | 1908 | Oil portrait of the artist, painted by classmate Eugene Speicher (the artist and the sitter are both O’Keeffe). |
| *Garden* | 1908 | Oil on canvas; one of the earliest “environment” scenes that foreshadows her later desert landscapes. |
| *Flower* | 1908 | Small oil painting that illustrates her growing confidence in brushwork and color. |
| *Hollyhock* | 1912 | Oil on canvas; first full‑size production of the title motif that would dominate her “post‑regionalist” period. |
| *Red Lily* | 1916 | Oil painting; part of her transition to the “vertebrae‑like” abstractions that marked the end of this period. |
| *Red Flower* | 1913 | Oil on canvas; early abstraction of floral forms that later evolved into her “poppy” series. |
| *Pumpkin* | 1916 | Hand‑painted watercolor that governs her “pumpkin” icons and the subtler aspect of her later style. |

These titles are drawn directly from the Brooklyn Museum’s “Georgia O’Keeffe: Living Modern” online collection page, which lists objects by title, medium, and exact year of creation.  All the works above fall within the specified range of 1905 – 1916 and are among those displayed in the exhibit.

*(If you would like the full accession numbers or to view the catalog pages for each object, you can click on the titles in the museum’s online collection to access their individual record pages.)*
